bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions".
bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent.

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a fee charged to oil and gas companies for methane emissions above specified thresholds.
Some electric utilities operate natural gas systems that could be subject to the emissions charge this resolution would nullify.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule published in November 2024. That rule established procedures for charging oil and gas companies an annual fee when their methane and other greenhouse gas emissions exceed certain thresholds. If enacted, the resolution would eliminate these compliance requirements and the associated emissions charge program.

bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S8395)

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects coal companies' access to federal coal leasing in Wyoming.
Coal mining operations would regain access to federal coal resources previously made unavailable for leasing.
Coal-fired power generators may be affected by changes in federal coal supply availability.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would overturn a 2024 Bureau of Land Management decision that made federal coal in Wyoming's Buffalo Field Office unavailable for future leasing. If passed, it would restore the earlier 2015 plan that allowed coal leasing in that area. The BLM had stopped offering coal leases after a court required the agency to evaluate climate impacts and consider alternatives to coal leasing.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on social media platforms and user-generated content websites.
New criminal prohibitions and mandatory restitution provisions would generate litigation and enforcement work related to intimate image publication.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. Social media platforms and similar websites would be required to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a complaint from the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 483.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects how Wyoming's permanent school fund generates revenue for public school support.
Expanding investment authority for the fund's principal would affect how financial institutions manage and invest these state trust assets.
The fund receives proceeds from school trust land sales and exchanges, affecting how these land transactions contribute to education funding.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would give Wyoming more flexibility in how it invests money from its permanent school fund, which was created when the state was formed using proceeds from federal land grants. Currently, Wyoming can only use interest earned from the fund to support public schools. The bill would allow the state to use broader earnings from investing the fund's principal, not just interest income.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Advanced Clean Cars II; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
subjects: Hybrid, electric, and advanced technology vehicles

industries.rationale: Automotive manufacturers would face different regulatory obligations depending on whether California's distinct emission standards remain in effect.
The Advanced Clean Cars II regulations affect the market for electric vehicle charging infrastructure and clean-energy vehicle adoption.
Electric utilities face demand changes tied to electric vehicle adoption rates influenced by state emission standards.
Petroleum refiners and distributors face market impacts from regulations that affect the mix of gasoline versus electric vehicles sold.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn an Environmental Protection Agency decision that allowed California to enforce its Advanced Clean Cars II regulations. Those regulations set emission standards for vehicles sold in California that differ from federal standards. If passed, the resolution would nullify the waiver that permits California to apply its own rules.

bill.title: Making National Parks Safer Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 469.

industries.rationale: The bill mandates installation of Next Generation 911 systems, which are internet-based telecommunications infrastructure that telecom providers typically supply and maintain.
NG911 systems are digital, internet protocol-based platforms requiring software, hardware, and IT services for implementation and operation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the National Park Service to assess the current state and costs of upgrading emergency call centers in national parks to Next Generation 911 systems. Based on that assessment, the Park Service must then develop a plan to install these modern, internet-based 911 systems at park emergency communications centers.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Motor Vehicle and Engine Pollution Control Standards; Heavy-Duty Vehicle and Engine Emission Warranty and Maintenance Provisions; Advanced Clean Trucks; Zero Emission Airport Shuttle; Zero-Emission Power Train Certification; Waiver of Preemption; Notice of Decision".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers, trucking companies, and motor carriers by determining whether they must comply with California's stricter emission standards.
Automotive and engine manufacturers would face different regulatory requirements depending on whether California's waiver stands or is nullified.
Zero-emission vehicle mandates affect demand for electric vehicle charging infrastructure and clean energy services for commercial fleets.
Requirements for zero-emission trucks and airport shuttles would influence electricity demand and infrastructure investment for fleet charging.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would block an Environmental Protection Agency decision that allowed California to enforce its own stricter emission standards for heavy-duty trucks and engines. The EPA had granted California a waiver from federal preemption rules, permitting the state to require cleaner trucks, zero-emission airport shuttles, and advanced clean truck standards. If passed, the resolution would nullify that waiver and prevent California from implementing these regulations.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.
Clinical trial enrollment requirements and expanded access to investigational drugs may affect hospitals and health systems conducting ALS research and treatment.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data more closely when awarding grants for experimental drug studies, and directs the Food and Drug Administration to publish five-year plans describing how it will help develop and approve treatments for these rare diseases. The bill also mandates reports evaluating the effectiveness of these grant programs.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

districtAwards.description: PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO SUPPORT CLOSING THE BROADBAND AVAILABILITY GAP AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIVE-YEAR ACTION PLAN.THE PROPOSED PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING PLANNING AND PRE-DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES: RESEARCH AND DATA COLLECTION, INCLUDING INITIAL IDENTIFICATION OF UNSERVED LOCATIONS AND UNDERSERVED LOCATIONS CONSISTENT WITH RULES, REGULATIONS, AND PROCESSES COMMISSION HAS ESTABLISHED FOR MAKING DETERMINATIONS IN BROADBAND DATA MAPS; PUBLICATIONS, OUTREACH, AND COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT; PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO POTENTIAL SUBGRANTEES, INCLUDING THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND EVENTS; ESTABLISHING, OPERATING, OR INCREASING CAPACITY OF A BROADBAND OFFICE THAT OVERSEES BROADBAND PROGRAMS AND BROADBAND DEPLOYMENT IN AN ELIGIBLE ENTITY; ASSET MAPPING ACROSS THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY TO CATALOGUE BROADBAND ADOPTION, AFFORDABILITY, EQUITY, ACCESS AND DEPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES OCCURRING WITHIN THE ELIGIBLE ENTITY; AND CONDUCTING SURVEYS OF UNSERVED, UNDERSERVED, AND UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND BARRIERS TO ADOPTION. EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS EXPECTED TO RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN THE BROADBAND OFFICE'S CAPACITY, DEVELOP THE 5-YEAR PLAN, INITIAL PROPOSAL, CHALLENGE PROCESS, AND FINAL PROPOSAL, AND PROVIDE AUDIT AND COMPLIANCE EXPERTISE THROUGHOUT THE BEAD PROGRAM'S PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE UNSERVED AND UNDERSERVED GROUPS IN THE STATE OF WYOMING WITH A FOCUS ON RURAL AND UNSERVED POPULATIONS.SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THE RECIPIENT DOES NOT INTEND TO INTEND TO SUBAWARD FUNDS.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation.
